voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: its questions (מאי, מיבעי ליה, למה לי, אטו, ותו ליכא, מנלן), its unattributed answers and derashot on new lemmas, the narrative of 12b.7-8, 13a.22-23, 16a.4-11, 16a.14, 16a.17, its kashya/teyuvta at 14a.9 and 15a.4
R' Elazar (ben Pedat): 12a.18, 13a.20, 13a.24-13b.6, and transmitter of R' Chanina at 15a.16-15b.6
Haman, whose words Rava (13b.16-19) and the stam's narrative (16a.4-10) report
Queen Esther, whose words R' Levi (15b.7-8) and the stam (16a.17) report
R' Chanina, whose dicta R' Elazar reports (15a.16-15b.6)
the Attribute of Justice, in R' Chanina's account (15b.5-6)
the Holy One, in R' Chanina's account (15b.5)
the R' Elazar in whose name Rabba bar Ofran reports, 'who heard from his teacher, and his teacher from his' (15b.10); not identified further

props.gloss_en: the verse: 'on the third day Esther put on royalty' (Esth 5:1) -- 'royal garments' would be expected
'and Mordechai knew all that was done' (Esth 4:1) -- what did he say? Rav: Haman has grown higher than Ahasuerus
Shmuel: the upper King has prevailed over the lower king
what is 'and the queen was greatly distressed' (Esth 4:4)? Rav: she began to menstruate
R' Yirmeya: she needed to relieve herself
'and Esther called Hatach' (Esth 4:5): Rav -- Hatach is Daniel; called Hatach because they cut him down (chatchuhu) from his greatness
Shmuel: because all matters of the kingdom were decided (nechtachin) by his word
Rav: because they cut him down from his greatness

'to know what this is and why this is' (Esth 4:5): R' Yitzchak -- she sent to him: perhaps Israel transgressed the five books of the Torah, of which it is written 'on this side and on that side they were written' (Ex 32:15)
'and they told Mordechai Esther's words' (Esth 4:12) -- but he [Hatach] did not go to him: hence one does not reply [bringing] bad news
'which is not according to the law' (Esth 4:16): R' Abba -- it was not according to the law, for every day until now [I went] under compulsion, and now willingly
'and if I perish, I perish' -- as I was lost from my father's house, so I will be lost to you
'and Mordechai passed' (Esth 4:17): Rav -- he made the first day of Passover pass in fasting
Shmuel: he crossed a stream of water
R' Elazar in R' Chanina's name: this teaches that the holy spirit clothed her -- here 'and she put on', there 'and the spirit clothed Amasai' (1 Chr 12:19)
never let a commoner's blessing be light in your eyes, for two commoners blessed two greats of their generation and it was fulfilled: David and Daniel
David, whom Aravna blessed (2 Sam 24:23); Daniel, whom Darius blessed: 'your God whom you serve continually will save you' (Dan 6:17)

let not a commoner's curse be light in your eyes: Avimelech cursed Sarah 'it is for you a covering of the eyes' (Gen 20:16), and it was fulfilled in her offspring: 'Isaac was old and his eyes dimmed' (Gen 27:1)

not like the Holy One's measure is that of flesh and blood: a man sets a pot and then puts water in it; the Holy One puts water and then sets the pot, to fulfil 'at the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heavens' (Jer 10:13)
whoever says a thing in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world, as said 'and Esther told the king in Mordechai's name' (Esth 2:22)
a righteous man lost is lost to his generation -- like a man who lost a pearl: wherever it is it is a pearl; it is lost only to its owner
'and all this is worth nothing to me' (Esth 5:13): when Haman saw Mordechai sitting at the king's gate he said: all this is worth nothing to me
Rav Chisda: this one [Mordechai] came as a prozbuli [rich man] and that one [Haman] as a prozbuti [poor man]
Rav Pappa: and they called him 'the slave sold for loaves'
'and all this is worth nothing to me' teaches that all that wicked one's treasures were engraved on his heart
the Holy One will in the future be a crown on the head of every righteous man, as said 'on that day the Lord of hosts will be a crown of glory' (Isa 28:5)
'for a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty' -- for those who do His will and await His glory; could it be for all? 'for the remnant of His people' -- for one who makes himself as a remnant

'and for a spirit of judgment' -- one who judges his inclination; 'who sits in judgment' -- who judges truly; 'and for strength' -- who overcomes his inclination; 'who turn back the battle' -- who give and take in Torah's battle; 'at the gate' -- scholars early and late in synagogues and study halls
the Attribute of Justice said before the Holy One: Master of the world, how are these different from those?
the Holy One: Israel engaged in Torah; the nations did not
it [the Attribute of Justice] said: 'these too erred through wine... they stumbled (paku) in judgment (peliliya)' (Isa 28:7) -- paku is Gehinnom (1 Sam 25:31), peliliya is judges (Ex 21:22)
'and she stood in the inner court of the king's house' (Esth 5:1): R' Levi -- when she reached the chamber of idols the Divine Presence left her

Esther: 'my God, my God, why have You forsaken me' (Ps 22:2)? do You judge the unwitting as the deliberate and the compelled as the willing? or is it because I called him 'dog' (Ps 22:21)? -- she then called him 'lion' (Ps 22:22)
'when the king saw Queen Esther' (Esth 5:2): R' Yochanan -- three ministering angels met her then: one raised her neck, one drew a thread of grace over her, one stretched the sceptre
and how much [was it stretched]? R' Yirmeya: it was two cubits and he made it twelve
and some say [he said]: sixteen
and some say: twenty-four
a baraita: sixty; and so you find with the arm of Pharaoh's daughter, and so with the teeth of the wicked
as written 'You broke the teeth of the wicked' (Ps 3:8), and Resh Lakish said: do not read 'shibarta' but 'shirbavta' [You enlarged]
Rabba bar Ofran in the name of R' Elazar, who heard it from his teacher and his teacher from his: two hundred
'up to half the kingdom' (Esth 5:3) -- half, not all of it, and not a thing that divides the kingdom: the building of the Temple
